extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, desired properties, and related criteria for Čech cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves and for projective/relative notions (projective morphisms, relative ampleness, base-point-freeness, quasiaffine, finite morphisms) in algebraic geometry. Focused on what cohomology should satisfy and equivalent characterizations used to produce or check these structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hi are covariant functors QCohX → ModA
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Hi (i ≥ 0) should be a covariant functor from the category of quasicoherent sheaves on X to A-modules (so H0 is Γ(X, −)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed as property (i); it grounds functoriality and ensures naturality of maps induced by maps of sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: H0 identified with global sections Γ
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor H0 should be identified with the global sections functor: H0(X, F) = Γ(X, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (ii). All constructions of cohomology must recover ordinary global sections at degree 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence associated to short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a short exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 of quasicoherent sheaves, there should be a long exact sequence in cohomology ... → H0(X,F) → H0(X,G) → H0(X,H) → H1(X,F) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (iii). The connecting homomorphisms must be definable; the long exact sequence is central for most cohomological arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality under morphisms (pullback/pushforward maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any quasicompact separated π : X → Y and F on X, there should be a natural morphism Hi(Y, π_* F) → Hi(X, F) extending the usual Γ map; and for G on Y a natural pullback Hi(Y, G) → Hi(X, π^*G) via adjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (iv). This yields the Leray spectral sequence later; the maps must be compatible with Γ and with compositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-base isomorphism: Hi(Y, π_*F) ≅ Hi(X,F) for affine π
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is an affine morphism (quasicompact separated assumptions included), then the natural map Hi(Y, π_*F) → Hi(X, F) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (v). This allows reducing cohomology calculations on arbitrary projective A-schemes to computations on projective space via affine embeddings/embeddings into P^n_A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine cover cohomology vanishing (Čech vanishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X can be covered by n affine open sets, then Hi(X, F) = 0 for i ≥ n for all quasicoherent F. In particular, on affine schemes all higher cohomology (i>0) vanishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (vi). This is the key vanishing used repeatedly (proved via Čech complexes for finite affine covers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology commutes with filtered colimits / direct sums
rubrics_metrics.description: Hi(X, colim_j F_j) = colim_j Hi(X, F_j); Hi behaves well under direct sums and filtered colimits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (vii). In module categories, filtered colimits are exact, which is used to prove this; important for building sheaves as colimits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit cohomology of O(m) on P^n_A
rubrics_metrics.description: For P^n_A and O(m): H^0(P^n_A, O(m)) is a free A-module of rank (n+m choose m) if m ≥ 0; H^n(P^n_A, O(m)) is free of rank (−m−1 choose −n−m−1) if m ≤ −n−1; and H^i(P^n_A, O(m)) = 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.2. This provides concrete dimensions/ranks and the first appearance of Serre duality and Hilbert-polynomial behavior; use as a basic computational rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness/coherence of cohomology for coherent sheaves on projective schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a projective A-scheme with A Noetherian and F a coherent sheaf on X, then Hi(X, F) is a coherent (i.e., finitely generated) A-module for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.3(i). This is a crucial finiteness criterion used in many finiteness/properness arguments and later coherence theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre vanishing (cohomology vanishes after twist)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a coherent sheaf F on a projective scheme X over A (A Noetherian), there exists N such that for all n ≥ N and all i > 0, Hi(X, F(n)) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.3(ii). Fundamental tool: twisting by large positive line bundle kills higher cohomology; used for surjections of global sections and to deduce properties of H^0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective morphisms: finite morphisms are projective
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite morphisms are projective: when Z → X is finite, one can realize Z ≅ Proj S for a suitable graded algebra S giving the projective structure. In particular, closed embeddings are projective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.F and surrounding text: constructive description via a graded algebra S with S0 ≅ O_X and S_n ≅ B for n≫0. Use to deduce closed embedding ⇒ projective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication chain: closed embedding ⇒ finite ⇒ projective ⇒ proper
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a chain of implications among morphism classes: closed embedding implies finite, finite implies projective, and projective implies proper (each implication is established or referenced in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these implications when checking or deducing properties of morphisms; converses may require hypotheses (e.g., Noetherian).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation theorem for projective morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Although projective morphisms are not 'reasonable' in the sense of §8.1, they satisfy a Cancellation Theorem: under appropriate hypotheses (e.g., composition with a projective map gives a projective composite), one can deduce projectivity of a factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.C points towards unwinding diagrams and using cancellation arguments (cf. exercise 11.2.A) — use diagrams and local affine arguments to verify projectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective + affine = finite (characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is projective and affine (with Y locally Noetherian), then π is finite; conversely finite morphisms are projective and affine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 18.1.5. Use coherence of π_* O_X and the characterization of finite type to check finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective + finite fibers (quasi-finite) = finite
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is projective and has finite fibers (equivalently quasi-finite) with Y Noetherian, then π is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.6. The proof uses localizing to an affine neighborhood and elimination theory (choose hypersurfaces missing fibers) to reduce to an affine projective case and then apply projective+affine=finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension for projective morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For a projective morphism π : X → Y with Y locally Noetherian, the set { q ∈ Y : dim π^{-1}(q) > k } is Zariski-closed; fiber dimension is upper semicontinuous on the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.1.B. This can be proved by arguments similar to Theorem 18.1.6 and is important for geometric intuition about family behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of H0 sequences after sufficiently large twist
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → F → G → H → 0 on a projective A-scheme with F coherent, for n≫0 the induced sequence 0 → H0(X, F(n)) → H0(X, G(n)) → H0(X, H(n)) → 0 is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.1.C. Use Serre vanishing (H^1(X, F(n)) = 0 for n≫0) to get surjectivity at H0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Čech cohomology via finite affine covers and independence of cover
rubrics_metrics.description: For quasicompact separated X, define Čech cohomology Hi_U(X,F) using a finite affine cover U; these groups are independent of the chosen finite affine cover and define Hi(X,F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem/Definition 18.2.2: prove independence by comparing covers differing by one open and using vanishing of higher Čech cohomology on affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Čech cohomology vanishes on affine schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affine A-scheme X and any quasicoherent F, the higher Čech cohomology Hi_U(X,F) vanishes for i>0 for any affine cover U (the extended Čech complex is exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.2.4. Proof uses partition-of-unity-style tricks, localization to distinguished opens D(f_i), and reduces to the case where one open equals X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of the Čech complex for finite affine covers
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a finite affine cover U = {U_i} of X, form the Čech complex 0 → ⨁_{|I|=1} F(U_I) → ⨁_{|I|=2} F(U_I) → ... with signed restriction maps; cohomology of this complex computes Hi_U(X,F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 18.2.1 and surrounding discussion. Maps are built from restrictions with sign conventions; check exactness properties from sheaf axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology commutes with base field extension (flat base change for fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X quasicompact separated over k and F quasicoherent, Hi(X,F) ⊗_k K ≅ Hi( X×_k Spec K, F ⊗_k K ) for any field extension K/k; thus hi(X,F) = hi(X⊗k K, F⊗k K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.2.H. The linear-algebra proof for fields generalizes to flat base change; useful to reduce statements to algebraically closed fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-point-freeness independent of extension of base field
rubrics_metrics.description: For quasicompact separated X over k and invertible sheaf L, L is base-point-free on X iff its pullback to X×_k Spec K is base-point-free for any field extension K/k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.2.I: follows from base-change for H0 (i=0) and behavior of bases under tensoring with K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatively globally generated (relative global generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y quasicompact quasiseparated and F quasicoherent on X, F is relatively globally generated (globally generated w.r.t π) if the natural map π^*π_*F → F is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §17.3.5 (relative setting). This condition is affine-local on Y and used to define base-point-free line bundles relative to π.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatively base-point-free (relative base-point-freeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free sheaf L on X is relatively base-point-free (base-point-free w.r.t π) if it is relatively globally generated (i.e., π^*π_*L → L is surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition immediately following relative global generation. Base-point-freeness gives canonical maps to projective bundles P(π_*L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative ampleness (π-ample) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on X is π-ample if for every affine open Spec B ⊂ Y, the restriction L|_{π^{-1}(Spec B)} is ample (equivalently absolutely ample on that preimage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition in §17.3.5 and surrounding remarks. π-ample implies π is quasicompact and separated; if π is projective, O(1) is π-ample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of π-ampleness (Theorem 17.3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y proper and quasicompact: (a) For some N>0, L^⊗N is π-very ample. (a') For all n≫0, L^⊗n is π-very ample. (b) For every finite-type quasicoherent sheaf F there exists n0 such that for n≥n0, F ⊗ L^⊗n is relatively globally generated. (c) L is π-ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 17.3.8. These equivalences are the working criteria used to verify relative ampleness in practice; they show ampleness can be checked by twisting and global generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful equivalent definition of very ampleness (17.3.I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under π proper and Y locally Noetherian (and π_*L finite type), L is very ample iff (i) L is relatively base-point-free and (ii) the canonical Y-morphism i : X → P(π_*L) is a closed embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.3.I. This yields an affine-local criterion for checking relative very ampleness (check on an affine cover of Y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample vector bundle definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free sheaf E on a proper A-scheme X is ample (as a vector bundle) if O_{P(E)/X}(1) is an ample invertible sheaf on the projective bundle P(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 17.3.9. This definition is compatible with the notion of ampleness for invertible sheaves; included for completeness though not used later in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiaffine schemes and morphisms: definitions and equivalent criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is quasiaffine if it admits a quasicompact open embedding into an affine scheme; equivalently the canonical map X → Spec Γ(X, O_X) is a quasicompact open embedding. A morphism π : X → Y is quasiaffine iff it is quasicompact and separated and the natural map X → Spec π_*O_X is a quasicompact open embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 17.3.10 and Exercise 17.3.J. Quasiaffineness is local on the target and preserved under base change and compositions; use the canonical map to global functions as the basic test.
